name: Technology Radar
description: Tech that is discussed in our engineering community, COPs, etc. and warrants further investigation should be added to our radar. This is based on Thoughtworks "build your own radar"

name: Temporal
description: We've identified durable execution and asynchronous workflow orchestration as a solution for some of our scalability & reliability issues, and Temporal is a platform that provides these capabilities

name: Python
description: Roughly half of our active services are written in Python, and it is the default choice for back-end and data work. The ecosystem around it — FastAPI, Pydantic, pytest, Ruff — is what our service templates generate, so choosing Python is also choosing a well-worn path through CI, deployment and testing.

name: TypeScript
description: TypeScript is our default for front-end applications and for the Node code around them, including infrastructure definitions and test suites. We don't write new plain JavaScript; the type checker earns its keep at the boundaries between our services.

name: FastAPI
description: FastAPI is the framework our new HTTP services are scaffolded with. It pairs naturally with Pydantic for request and response models, gives us OpenAPI documentation for free, and runs happily in Lambda behind Mangum. Django remains in a handful of older services but is not where new work goes.

name: Pydantic
description: Pydantic is how we validate data crossing a boundary — HTTP payloads, event messages, and configuration via pydantic-settings. Used in a large share of our Python services, well beyond just the FastAPI ones. Parse, don't validate: model the shape once and let it fail loudly at the edge.

name: React
description: React is the standard for our customer-facing and internal web applications, with a shared component library so that our applications look and behave like one product rather than several.

name: pytest
description: pytest is the test framework for essentially every Python repository we have — the most consistently adopted tool in our estate. Fixtures and parametrisation keep test code close in style across services, which matters when engineers move between them.

name: New Relic
description: New Relic is our observability platform, instrumented across most services and wired in at deploy time rather than bolted on afterwards. One place to answer "is it broken, and where" is worth more than the best individual tool in each category.

name: CircleCI
description: CircleCI runs continuous integration for the large majority of our repositories, and our service templates ship with a working config. GitHub Actions is used for a small number of specific jobs, but CircleCI is the default and new services should not need to think about it.

name: Serverless Framework
description: Serverless Framework defines and deploys most of our Lambda services, with a serverless.yml sitting alongside the application code. Adopt on weight of use rather than enthusiasm: the v4 licence change is worth keeping an eye on, and it is a reason to revisit this blip rather than a reason to move off it today.

name: Ruff
description: Ruff is our Python linter and formatter, configured in our service template as the single tool for both. It has largely displaced Black and isort; where you still find Black in an older repository, moving to Ruff is a safe tidy-up.

name: uv
description: uv is our Python package and project manager, and the direction of travel for every Python repository. It is already the most common choice across our services and is what our FastAPI service template generates. Resolves and installs fast enough that CI and local setup stop being something you work around, and it replaces the pip/pipenv/virtualenv pile with one tool.

name: Pipenv
description: Pipenv still manages dependencies in a substantial minority of our Python repositories, but we are deliberately moving away from it in favour of uv. Don't start a new service with it, and prefer migrating when you are already working in a repository that uses it.

name: Docker
description: Docker gives us a reproducible way to run services and their dependencies locally, and is how we package the services that run as containers on ECS rather than as Lambda functions. Being serverless-first doesn't remove the need for containers: it makes it worth being deliberate about which of the two a service needs.

name: Terraform
description: Terraform is how we manage shared and long-lived infrastructure that doesn't belong to a single service's serverless.yml — networking, data stores, and account-level resources. Click-ops changes in the AWS console are not a substitute.

name: Native mobile development
description: We build our customer apps natively — Kotlin on Android, Swift on iOS — rather than through a cross-platform framework. The cost is two codebases and two skill sets; what we get back is immediate access to platform capabilities and no dependency on a third party keeping pace with OS releases. We generate our API clients rather than hand-writing them, which keeps the duplication between the two apps in the UI layer.

name: Claude Code
description: Claude Code is in everyday use across a large share of our repositories, most of which now carry a CLAUDE.md describing how to work in them. Treat that file as part of the codebase: the quality of what the agent produces tracks the quality of the context you give it, and a stale CLAUDE.md is worse than none.
